service.description: Whether an address (or a server) signs in with a provider this server is set up for (mr-moqui docs/interfaces/Mail-OAuth.md): oauthProviderEnumId when given (discover#EmailServer's, or the account server's), else the provider org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.find#OAuthProvider finds for the address's domain or the incoming server's host (no network: no MX lookup); configured as get#OAuthProviders says (a client of this deployment, not disabled); providerLabel names the button (Sign in with Google, with Microsoft); offersPop when the provider has a POP server here (its EmailOAuthProvider popHost), so the wizard may offer to read the mail over POP. choice is null when no provider has the mail, and when this host has no mail client. The account page and the wizard still render.

The add-account wizard's servers for an address, and where they came from: a provider IronStone knows (get#MailProvider, with its app-password help), else org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.discover#EmailServer (Thunderbird autoconfig and its ISPDB, DNS SRV records, else the guesses imap.domain and smtp.domain). A reserved domain (example.com, .example, .test, .invalid, .localhost, .local) is never looked up: it gets the guesses at once. A discovery that fails falls back to the guesses, said so (logged). The servers are in the wizard's terms: storeKind imap or pop, storeSecurity and smtpSecurity ssl, starttls or none; smtpUsername is the outgoing server's own user when discovery says it signs in as another one than the incoming (the Connect step's outgoing sign-in, prefilled). oauthProviderEnumId is the provider discovery found the mail at (for a company domain at Google or Microsoft, by its MX hosts), for get#OAuthChoice.

The MailAccounts list: the user's Internal account first (not removable), then each mail account they own or share (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.get#UserEmailAccounts) with what the list shows: kind, status (active, syncing, paused, setup not finished, sign-in failed, sync failed, local only) with its color and problem text, last sync, unread, outbox failures, the servers (to a manager; never the password), members of a shared account and what the user may do. Each account stands alone: one that fails is logged by name, listed with what is known and named in failedParts.

One account for its page (MailAccounts/Account): the list's view of it (get#MailAccountList), its folders with their kind (folderKindEnumId, kindByUser when the user chose it), the server's path, counts and whether the sync reads it (subscribed; the Inbox always), and for a manager the servers in the wizard's terms (storeKind, storeSecurity, storeHost, storePort, smtpHost, smtpPort, smtpSecurity, mailUsername and hasPassword; smtpUsername and hasSmtpPassword, the outgoing server's own sign-in when it has one; never a password), the members of a shared account, the options and the provider's help. signIn says how a manager's account signs in (get#OAuthStatus: isOAuth, signedIn, needsSignIn, signInDate) and oauth whether it may sign in with Google or Microsoft here (get#OAuthChoice: providerLabel, configured). found is false, with "not found", for an account the user does not reach.

The wizard's Connect step and the account page's sign-in and servers: make the account (paused until the wizard's Finish, so the sync job leaves it alone) or change the one the user manages. The servers come in the wizard's terms (storeKind imap or pop, storeSecurity ssl or starttls, smtpSecurity ssl, starttls or none; a port left empty takes the usual one for its security); the user name defaults to the address. A password is needed to make an account with a password, and an empty one keeps the one stored; a password given makes the account sign in with it (EatPassword: an account that signed in with a provider is signed out there). With authTypeEnumId EatOAuth2 and oauthProviderEnumId no password is taken: a new account is made to sign in with the provider later (the wizard's own sign-in makes its account through start#MailSignIn, by the framework, once the sign-in succeeds), on the servers given or else the provider's own (its EmailOAuthProvider row: the IMAP server, or with storeKind pop its POP server, popHost, refused when it has none), and an account there already keeps its servers and its sign-in, which the provider's sign-in sets (storeKind given moves it between the provider's IMAP and POP servers).
The outgoing server's own sign-in (smtpUsername, smtpPassword: a provider whose SMTP takes another user than its incoming server) is tried first (test#MailAccount, SMTP only, on the servers just saved) and stored only when the server takes it; refused, nothing of the save is kept and the error says what the server answered. An empty smtpUsername makes SMTP sign in as the incoming server does again; the same user with no password keeps the one stored. Not for an account that signs in with a provider.
accountKindEnumId: a new account's kind (EakExternal, the default, EakShared, or EakHosted); given for an account there it changes the kind (update#EmailAccount, by the framework's rules: personal again only when one person is left on it). gatewayDelivery makes a hosted or shared account with no mail server and no password, so the SMTP listener delivers its mail (a personal account cannot; an account that already has a server keeps it, and the listener then leaves the mail to the sync). Strict on access: an emailAccountId the user does not manage is not found.

parameter.name: passwordOnly
parameter.description: Only the password changes (the Fix of a sign-in that failed)

parameter.name: authTypeEnumId
parameter.description: EatPassword, or EatOAuth2 for an account that signs in with oauthProviderEnumId

parameter.name: gatewayDelivery
parameter.description: Hosted or shared, delivered by the gateway: no mail server and no password

service.description: Begin an account's sign-in with Google or Microsoft (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.start#OAuthSignIn, in the popup of the SignIn screen; mr-moqui docs/interfaces/Mail-OAuth.md), on a provider this server is set up for (get#OAuthChoice). From the wizard (setup) with no account yet, the address, name and kind go to start#OAuthSignIn, which makes the account only when the sign-in succeeds: paused with the year's sync window until the wizard's Finish, as one with a password; its emailAccountId comes with the sign-in's outcome (get#OAuthStatus). storeKind pop (the wizard's choice) makes it read the Inbox over POP: start#OAuthSignIn storeProtocol pop3, on the provider's POP server (popHost; refused when it has none), and the sign-in asks for the provider's POP scope too (popScope: Microsoft's POP.AccessAsUser.All; Google's mail scope covers POP); nothing is made when the sign-in does not finish. The wizard coming back to an account it made changes it first (its kind, IMAP or POP). From the account page (no setup) the account the user manages signs in again, or for the first time instead of a password. allowAddressChange is the user's yes to a sign-in as another address (the account takes the address). The sign-in itself, its state and its tokens are the framework's: authUrl is for the popup, signInId for get#OAuthStatus.

parameter.name: storeKind
parameter.description: imap or pop, for the wizard's account

service.description: Sign in to an account's servers (manage permission; org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.test#EmailAccount): each step (sending, receiving, folders) with what it said, and for a failure what it most likely means and what to try (an app password, the port and security, the host name, a firewall, IMAP access turned off), with the provider's help. testStore false tries only the outgoing server; smtpUsername and smtpPassword are an outgoing sign-in to try instead of the stored one (nothing is stored). folderMap is how the folders map to Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Spam, Trash and Archive here: the account's own choice of a folder (update#EmailFolder) over the server's special use, with the server's folder for the kind when the two differ (serverPath); folderList is each server folder with its kind on the server and here and whether the sync reads it.

Send a test message from an account to its own address (send permission; org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.send#TestMessage), and say when it comes back: an account still in the wizard (paused, never synced) gets it with its first sync after Finish; a paused one when it is resumed; any other with its next sync (its interval, else every few minutes, or Sync now). A send that fails answers sent false and resultText with what the server said; nothing is left in the Outbox.

The wizard's Options step and the account page's options (manage permission): the account's name, color, sync window (days; empty for all mail), sync interval, filing policy (ErfLinkedOnly: only the mail the user links goes on a record; ErfAllMatches: every message with a known contact) and kind, personal (EakExternal), shared (EakShared) or hosted (EakHosted), by the framework's rules (update#EmailAccount: shared at any time, personal again only when one person is left on it; when the kind changes and the filing given is the one the account had, it follows the new kind's default), and for a shared account the users to add as members (add#EmailAccountUser), each on its own: one that is refused (an unknown user, the owner) is logged and named in failedMemberList. They are added in the caller's transaction: the update above holds the account's row, so a member row in a transaction of its own would wait on it.

The wizard's Finish (manage permission): the account becomes active. One with an incoming server starts its first sync on a service worker as the user (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.sync#EmailAccount); the sync job keeps it in sync from then on. One with no incoming server (hosted here, or shared and delivered by the gateway) becomes active and no sync starts. syncStarted is false when no sync was started, and, logged, when the sync could not start (the job starts it within minutes).
Pause an account's sync, or resume it (manage permission).

actions.script: ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.update#EmailAccount').parameters({emailAccountId: emailAccountId, statusId: paused ? 'EasPaused' : 'EasActive'}).call()

service.description: The user's own accounts removed with their mail kept (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.get#EmailAccountAccess includeRemoved: the owner's only, never a member's), for the account list's Removed accounts: the name, the address, how many messages are kept here and when it last synced.

Delete one of the user's removed accounts with its mail kept here (delete#EmailAccount, which deletes a removed account for its owner only, always with its mail; a message another record still refers to is kept, out of the account). Only a removed account: an account in use is removed from its own page.

actions.script: const access = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.get#EmailAccountAccess').parameters({emailAccountId: emailAccountId, includeRemoved: true}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return const account = access?.account if (!account || !account.isRemoved || !account.isOwner) { ec.message.addError(ec.resource.expand('Email account ${id} not found', '', {id: emailAccountId})); return } const out = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.delete#EmailAccount').parameters({emailAccountId: emailAccountId, deleteLocalCopies: true}).call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return deletedMessageCount = out?.deletedMessageCount || 0 keptMessageCount = out?.keptMessageCount || 0 message = ec.resource.expand(keptMessageCount ? '${name} deleted with ${deleted} messages; ${kept} filed on records are kept' : '${name} deleted with its mail', '', {name: account.accountName || account.emailAddress, deleted: deletedMessageCount, kept: keptMessageCount})

service.description: The accounts whose sync progress the screens show (the topic emailSyncProgress of org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.sync#EmailAccount, sent to the account's owner and members): the user's mail accounts with a server, by id with their names, and which are syncing now. emailAccountId narrows it to one.

The Identities screen: each mail account the user may send from (not the Internal one), with its identities (name, address, reply-to, signature, its placement, default) and whether the user manages it (only a manager changes them; org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices create, update and delete#EmailIdentity check it).

actions.script: const L = (text) => text.length > 255 ? text : ec.l10n.localize(text) accountList = [] const users = ec.service.sync().name('org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.get#UserEmailAccounts').call() if (ec.message.hasError()) return const textOf = (html) => String(html || '').replace(/<br\s*\/?>/gi, ' · ').replace(/<\/p>\s*<p[^>]*>/gi, ' · ').replace(/<[^>]*>/g, ' ') .replace(/ /g, ' ').replace(/&/g, '&').replace(/</g, '<').replace(/>/g, '>').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() for (const account of Array.from(users?.accountList || [])) { if (account.isInternal || !account.canSend) continue const identities = Array.from(account.identityList || []) accountList.push({emailAccountId: account.emailAccountId, accountName: account.accountName || account.emailAddress, emailAddress: account.emailAddress, canManage: account.canManage === true, identityRows: identities.map((identity) => ({emailIdentityId: identity.emailIdentityId, emailAccountId: account.emailAccountId, displayName: identity.displayName || '', emailAddress: identity.emailAddress || '', replyToAddress: identity.replyToAddress || '', signatureHtml: identity.signatureHtml || '', signatureText: textOf(identity.signatureHtml).substring(0, 120) || L('No signature'), signaturePlacementEnumId: identity.signaturePlacementEnumId || 'EspBelowQuote', placementText: identity.signaturePlacementEnumId === 'EspAboveQuote' ? L('above the quote') : L('below the quote'), useForReplies: identity.useForReplies ? 'Y' : 'N', isDefault: identity.isDefault ? 'Y' : 'N', nameText: (identity.displayName ? identity.displayName + ' <' + identity.emailAddress + '>' : identity.emailAddress) || '', defaultText: identity.isDefault ? L('Default') : '', canManage: account.canManage === true, canDelete: account.canManage === true && identities.length > 1}))}) }

service.description: Add an identity to an account, or change one (manage permission, checked by the framework's identity services). The signature is cleaned as safe HTML (the rich-text editor's markup) whatever the client sends.

The OutOfOffice screen: the accounts the user manages (not the Internal one) with whether their automatic reply is on now, and the chosen account's reply (emailAccountId, else the first) for the form, from org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.get#EmailOutOfOffice, with who gets it (replyAudienceEnumId: EraEveryone, EraContacts, EraInternal; who is a contact is the hook BossSetupData sets, STRT_EMAIL_CONTACT_SERVICE) and the more domains whose senders count as inside the organization (internalDomains, shown comma and space). Each account's state stands alone: one that fails is logged and shown as unknown.

Set an account's automatic reply (manage permission, checked by store#EmailOutOfOffice), with who gets it (replyAudienceEnumId: EraEveryone, EraContacts for contacts and people inside, EraInternal for people inside only) and the more domains of people inside (internalDomains, separated by commas or spaces), or with applyToAll the same reply on every account the user manages that has a server, each on its own in a transaction of its own (one that fails is logged and named in failedList). The messages are cleaned as safe HTML. Dates are yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm in the user's zone.

The TextBlocks screen: the text blocks the user may use (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.find#EmailTextBlocks: their own and those shared with a group they are in), matching searchText, with who shares each and whether the user may change it (only its owner); and the user's groups to share with.

Add a text block of the user's, or change one of their own (create and update#EmailTextBlock check the owner and that the user is in the group shared with). The body is cleaned as safe HTML; a shortcut is a word without spaces or a leading slash.

The Rules screen: the rules the user may change, in order (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices.find#EmailRules), each with its conditions and actions as a sentence and whether it is a blocked sender (block#Sender's rule: from is an address, to Spam); the accounts the user manages (not the Internal one) with their folders and labels for the rule editor and for Run now; and the blocked senders.

Add a rule of the user's, or change one they may change (create and update#EmailRule, which check the account and normalize the conditions and actions: normalize#EmailRule says what is wrong). conditionsJson and actionsJson are the lists as JSON text, as the Rules editor sends them.

The Rules editor's Test: a rule as it is in the editor (conditionsJson, matchAllEnumId; emailRuleId when it is a saved rule, which must be one the user may change) tried on the newest limit messages of a folder (emailFolderId, else the Inbox of emailAccountId) without acting on them (org.moqui.impl.EmailClientServices test#EmailRule: no action runs, the rule's count stays). matchList: each message it matches with its subject, sender and date in the user's words, newest first, and what opens its thread in the Inbox as the framework answers it (store, threadId, rootEmailMessageId, emailAccountId, emailFolderId): threadKey (email:threadId, the Inbox's thread parameter) and inboxUrl (the folder with the thread open); resultText counts them.

The Mail box of Commons Preferences (design-drawers-commons.md §11 MailDefaults), from the user preferences the Inbox and Compose read (ironstone.comms.InboxServices.get#InboxData, ComposeServices): MAIL_READING_PANE (right, bottom, off), MAIL_ARCHIVE_NEXT (N to go back to the list after archive), MAIL_MARK_READ_SECONDS, MAIL_UNDO_SECONDS (10 by default), MAIL_REMOTE_IMAGES (always, else ask: each sender's pictures are allowed in the reading pane), MAIL_CONVERSATION (threads, or messages: the Inbox lists mail one message at a time), MAIL_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT (the account Compose starts from, empty for the first account), MAIL_SIGNATURE_PLACEMENT (above or below the quote) and MAIL_SWIPE_LEFT / MAIL_SWIPE_RIGHT (archive, trash, read, unread, flag or spam: the phone list runs that action). accountOptions is the accounts the user may send from, for the default-account field; a failure listing them leaves the choices empty and the rest of the box still loads.

Save the Mail box of Commons Preferences: the user preferences get#MailDefaults reads, each checked against its choices. A value not given is left as it is. An empty default account clears MAIL_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT.
